117696.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Staten Island
117696.note: Lubavitch.com (21 Sept 2005): 'Rabbi Moshe and Chani Katzman, Chabad's representatives in Staten Island, lived in the Oakwood Heights neighborhood when they first moved to the Island over 18 years ago' (so 1987 or a little before). Medium: a count back. Now 289 Harold Street (Bais Menachem).

earlier.where: the Oakwood Heights neighborhood (where the Katzmans first lived)

117915.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Westchester County
117915.note: Rabbi Velvl Butman's own biography: after shlichus internships from the mid-1980s he was 'appointed to direct Lubavitch activities in Westchester County, New York. There he has served with distinction since 1993, founding 11 outreach centers'. Medium: his own page; the Jewish Week (2018) quotes the Westchester Jewish Council: 'In the last two decades, Westchester has seen a growth from one Chabad center to 10'. The listing now names Mrs. Rochel Butman.

119714.name: United Lubavitcher Yeshivoth
119714.note: The Ocean Parkway branch of Tomchei Tmimim (Chabadpedia): a building was first planned on Maple Street, Crown Heights (cornerstone 1963; JTA, 10 June 1963: ground broken for a $2,000,000 complex for the United Lubavitcher Yeshivoth's new headquarters), but 'the deteriorating condition of the Crown Heights neighborhood led to the abandonment of this plan' and it was built on Ocean Parkway instead. No year found for the move; its listing is in the first online directory (2004).

117689.name: Melville & Huntington Chabad Center
117689.note: Mikvah.org (a news item, undated): 'Rabbi Asher Vaisfiche, director of Chabad of Huntington since he established the center together with his wife Miriam in 1991'. Medium: one source, read through a search summary (the text is not in the page's plain HTML). Now 498 Sweet Hollow Rd., Melville.
